tools.name: triz_matrix
tools.description: Look up the canonical contradiction matrix for an improving and worsening engineering parameter. Blank and diagonal cells fail closed; never guess a recommendation.

tools.description: Multi-parameter contradiction lookup: every (improving x worsening) matrix cell with the principles aggregated by how many cells recommend each (ties broken by mean position). tools.name: triz_build_model
tools.description: Build a typed function model from an interaction table: components with stable ids, names and roles, and subject/action/object interactions with explicit carrier descriptors and polarities. Generates readable, stable ports and wire ids: each interaction gets its own input port on its object, `in:<carrier>:<subject>:<action>`, so no input port is fed by two functions (no fan-in, no extensive-fan-in); each subject gets one output port per carrier it sends, `out:<carrier>`, shared by its functions on that carrier (fan-out: one shared level when intensive, the sum of the demands when extensive); each function is the wire `wire:<subject>:<action>:<object>:<carrier>`. Each part is percent-escaped (':' as %3A, '%' as %25), so distinct tuples never share an id. Validates the result, runs lints, and returns a bounded completeness report of unrecorded component pairs, isolation and product reach. Ratings and behavior are never inferred. Optional flows reference component and carrier ids from the table.

tools.name: triz_function_model
tools.description: Check a TRIZ function model written as a typed wiring diagram (boxes with typed ports, wires carrying one carrier and a polarity) and analyse it: harm loops (closed loops containing a harmful or excessive function, with witness cycles), an ideality profile per resource dimension (never summed; a scalar ratio only with explicit weights), separation checks for embedded physical contradictions, and, given compare_to, a componentwise baseline-vs-concept comparison plus an isomorphism check: whether the two models share a wiring shape ignoring every id and label (a bijection preserving roles, port sides, shared carriers, wiring, ratings, and costs; decided:false if the bounded search runs out). With mpv_weights (and compare_to), comparison.mpv compares the two models over the main parameters of value only: the named cost dimensions or 'harmful', componentwise and by the explicit weighted sum, listing the other axes on which they differ; a lost deliverable still decides, and no weight is ever filled in. Each verdict cites the theorem in theory/CategoricalTriz.lean it relies on (basis). Any dangling, mis-directed, or mistyped wire, or an invalid embedded contradiction, fails closed with ok:false. Harm loops and separation read the outer wiring and the model's own contradictions only: when boxes declare an `inner` model, incompleteHierarchy lists them, the note says their inner loops and contradictions are not analysed, and the isomorphism check carries incompleteHierarchy: true; run triz_expand_hierarchy on each first. Loops are hypotheses about mechanism to substantiate, not findings.

tools.name: triz_flow
tools.description: Flow analysis (router entry 16) over the model's declared `flows`: each an ordered path of the boxes a carrier passes through, in series, which functions do not record (two valves in series both act on the water, not on each other). Per flow: its steps (consecutive boxes, with the functions of the flow's carrier between them; declaredOnly counts the steps no function joins); bottleneck candidates (the performer of an insufficient, excessive, or harmful function that carries the flow's carrier and touches the path: a resistance-like output on the flow, at its position); accumulation candidates (a box where the steps of every flow of the carrier converge, with at least two predecessors and fewer successors, or a last box inside the engineered system, role tool or mediator, that no flow of the carrier continues from); leak candidates (a function on the carrier from a box on the path to an environment or supersystem box off it); loops (a box that recurs on the path, with the cycle between occurrences); and the harm loops that meet the path. Every item is a structural candidate to substantiate, not a finding. Boxes consecutive on a flow are adjacent for triz_transform merge. A model that fails the type-check, flows included, fails closed.

tools.name: triz_transform
tools.description: Apply one typed model transformation and return the new model. Principle constructions: segment (1: divide a box into parts whose ports partition its ports), take_out (2: separate the ports touching a harmful or excessive function, or isolate the part carrying all useful functions), merge (5: collapse adjacent or identical boxes into one; boxes consecutive on a declared flow are adjacent), standby (11: add an unwired typed absorber for a box's functions), reverse (13: swap a function's performer and object), rerate (16: rate a useful function insufficient or excessive; 23: change the level of a function on a cycle), retarget (22: a harmful function's source feeds a useful function), feedback (23: add a function that closes a loop), interpose (24: route a function through a new mediator box), cheap_copy (26, 27: replace a box by a cheaper copy with the same ports). Also trim (perform a typed-feasible trim, re-attaching each kept function to an absorber; rule B is Principle 25, one absorber for everything is Principle 6) and rewrite (delete and add boxes and wires; no remaining wire may touch a deleted box). Every result type-checks or the call fails closed with ok:false. When the segmented box declares behaviour, segment (and take_out) reports behaviourallyIndependent: whether the box's relation is the product of its projections onto the parts; if so each part gets its projection, else no part gets behaviour and each coupled part is named with a witness: two rows whose mix is not a row. It also suggests the finest partition of the box's ports over which its relation is a product (behavior.finest: parts; cut, the suggested blocks the given parts cut, empty iff the split holds; splitsFurther, when nothing is cut, the parts that hold several blocks; decided:false past the cap). interpose's mediator may declare behavior (rows, or 'identity'). A transformation is a structural move, not evidence that it solves the problem: model the result and compare it with triz_function_model compare_to, or with triz_behavior compare_to when behaviour is declared, passing the boxMap that segment, take_out, or cheap_copy returns as box_map. merge renames the merged ports to '<box>.<port>', so no box_map recovers a merged product box's deliverables: they read as lost and regained. reverse returns undo, a rewrite that restores the original model, added ports included.

tools.name: triz_rule_apply
tools.description: Double-pushout rewriting with rules as data. A rule is a span L ← K → R of patterns over the function-model schema (boxes with ports typed by carrier variables, and wires); pass it as `rule`, or name a built-in evolution-line rule with `rule_id`: 'mono-bi' (transition to supersystem, mono → bi; apply again for poly), 'feedback' (increasing controllability, self-adjusting with feedback; bind its carrier variable 's' with `carriers`), or 'working-field' (changing the working field: the matched function re-made on another carrier; bind 'd' with `carriers` to a carrier other than the matched one; the result's fieldChanges records both carriers' layer and dimension). Each built-in rule cites the evolution-trends.md line it encodes. `rule_id` 'uneven-development' is a detector, not a rewrite, and takes only the model: the lagging subsystem, a box of the largest harm-loop region that is also on a binding feasibility dimension or limits a deliverable (feasibility finds it unprovidable, or it performs an insufficient function on a product); verdict lagging, none, or undecided (no harm loop, or feasibility undecided). Without `match`: lists every injective match of L (seed it with `at`), each verified as a typed homomorphism and marked applicable when the no-identification and no-dangling conditions hold (a deleted box may not lie on a declared flow) and the rule's `distinct` carrier variables bind different carriers; decided:false if the step budget runs out, complete:false past `limit`. A rule's `forbid` holds negative application conditions (Habel–Pennemann): each pattern extends `left` by id, and a match that extends to an occurrence of one — including any elements the pattern adds — is not applicable; a condition its own step budget cannot decide also refuses the application. With `match` (a listed match, or your own mapping): checks the match, these conditions, and that a kept box keeps the ports its declared rows name (every port for behavior and transition; the named ports for feasibility), then deletes the image of L \ K, glues R \ K under fresh ids, and returns the new model, which type-checks or the call fails closed; deliverableKeysChanged says a deliverable moved to another port or carrier. A rule application is a structural move, not evidence that it helps: compare the result with triz_function_model compare_to.

tools.name: triz_behavior
tools.description: Compose declared box behaviour (carrier `values`, box `behavior` rows) into the model's external relation: boundary inputs (unwired input ports) to deliverables (product input ports fed by a non-harmful function). The default upstream scope composes boxes that can reach a deliverable and explicitly assumes omitted boxes accept everything; scope whole composes every box, including downstream and disconnected constraints. full_relation returns all rows within the search cap. Feedback loops compose by the relational trace, so every consistent steady state counts, and the steady states are listed. `factorisations` lists each composed box whose relation is the product of its projections onto two or more groups of ports, with the finest groups, in box order (decided:false past a per-box cap): segment it into them, or unions of them, and each part keeps its projection. The hint describes the declared rows, not a physical split, and changes no verdict. This is steady-state semantics, not dynamics. With `compare_to`, decide whether the model (a concept, e.g. a triz_transform result) has the baseline's input→deliverable relation; pass segment's or take_out's boxMap as `box_map`. `trim` is shorthand: perform the trim as triz_transform does and compare the result with the model. Verdict preserved; changed (a lost deliverable, or a counterexample input with the differing outputs and which relation contains which); or undecided (reason missing-behavior: the boxes that can reach a deliverable and declare no behaviour; reason no-steady-state: neither model has a steady state at any input, so equal empty relations say nothing). With `weakest_spec` (and compare_to or trim), give the weakest box specification (residual in Rel) for the one box of the concept that can reach a deliverable and declares no behaviour, against the same target: spec, every row of that box whose composite stays inside the target, with preserves:true when declaring it gives exactly the target (any behaviour that does is contained in it); impossible, when the spec's composite misses part of the target (an uncovered input is given; no behaviour of that box gives the target, and the empty relation, which always stays inside, is never read as preserving) or a deliverable is lost; undecided for three or more boxes without behaviour (several-holes), missing baseline behaviour, an empty target, or past the cap (state-cap). When the box to specify declares `producible` rows (what it can physically produce), the spec is the residual cut down to them: spec when that still covers the target (producible.infeasible lists the residual rows left out); impossible with reason infeasible when the residual covers the target but its producible rows do not, with requiredInfeasible giving, per missing target pair, the residual rows that deliver it, none producible (every relation that gives the target contains one of each); impossible with reason not-covered when the residual itself does not cover. With exactly two boxes without behaviour (boxes), a pair of relations stays inside the target iff every pair of rows, one of each, does, and the maximal such pairs are the formal concepts of the safe row pairs: spec lists those whose composite covers the target (specs, each declared and re-checked to give exactly the target; every pair that gives the target lies inside one), with weakest:true when there is one and weakest:false when several are incomparable; impossible (not-covered) when none covers, with each maximal pair's uncovered input (pairs); undecided (concept-cap) past the cap on concepts. Producible rows cut each box first; impossible with reason infeasible then means some pair over all rows (wouldGive) would give the target. Fails closed on ill-typed behaviour, an ambiguous or mismatched box_map, inputs whose values differ between the models, and past the state cap. With `certificate: true` and compare_to or trim, supported comparisons return a request-bound Lean equality with nonemptiness or an input/output pair belonging to only one relation; declared box_map, one-sided inputs and gained deliverables follow the comparison's baseline interface and selected scope. With row_costs in the one-hole mode, cheapestExtension gives an exact least-cost set of safe nonproducible rows to add, using the complete target relation and explicit integer costs, or reports an undecided capped search; it is not-applicable (target-not-covered-by-residual) when the residual itself misses the target, and row_costs fail with invalid-row-costs wherever no one-box residual is computed; the Boolean verdict is unchanged. The verdict holds for the relations as declared; substantiating them, the absorber's or mediator's first, is outside the kernel.

tools.name: triz_weakness
tools.description: Rank candidate concepts that declare behaviour by the operating situations they admit (references/weakness.md). A situation is a valuation of the concepts' boundary inputs (unwired input ports, matched by box and port id) over their carriers' declared values: the declared input space is weakness.md's list of operating situations. A concept admits a situation when it has a steady state there and every deliverable output there is acceptable (`acceptable`: per deliverable port, or per carrier for all its deliverables, the values that are, listed or derived from a threshold `at_least`/`below` that is a declared level of the carrier; required for every deliverable; derived sets are listed under acceptable in the result). Give each operating condition the same box and port id in every concept (e.g. an environment box with an unwired input); readByOne lists the inputs only one concept reads. Ranked by set inclusion: weakest (admits everything any other admits), maximal, and every pair as equal, first-weaker, second-weaker, or incomparable, with a situation only one admits each way. The admitted count is a secondary figure: it depends on how finely carrier values are declared. `priors` gives a real prior over the situations (weakness.md: a real prior beats the uniform assumption): per situation input (box and port), or per carrier, a nonnegative weight per declared value (unlisted inputs and values count 1; 0 rules a value out); each concept carries the total prior mass of what it admits (weightedAdmitted, ranked in byWeight), and no inclusion ever moves under weights. `joint_prior` is the alternative for correlated operating conditions: an explicit complete joint table, a weight for every situation (zero allowed), with no independence assumption; it reports jointAdmittedWeight and jointAdmittedProbability per concept, ranked in byJointPrior, separately from inclusion and counts. Give priors or joint_prior, not both. Fails closed when the concepts deliver different ports, an input several read ranges over different values, or acceptable misses a deliverable or names an undeclared value, or a prior is malformed; undecided on missing behaviour or past the state cap. Filter concepts for adequacy first; for safety, integrity, or authorisation decisions admitting more is the wrong direction. With `certificate: true`, also returns a Lean file that encodes each concept's rows and proves every equal, incomparable, or strictly ordered pair: inclusion one way and not the other (AtLeastAsWeak) and the strictly larger count (card_lt_of_strictly_weaker), decided over every valuation; past its cap, `certificate` gives the reason there is none. Prior mass is not certified.

tools.name: triz_dynamics
tools.description: Bounded dynamics of a function model whose boxes declare `state`, `initial`, and `transition` rows (state, inputs) → (next state, outputs): each such box is a nondeterministic Mealy machine (a lens with a residual is one, with the residual as state); boxes with `behavior` are stateless. Boxes compose synchronously along the wiring: wires are instantaneous, memory lives only in declared state, and a loop through stateless boxes resolves within a step as in triz_behavior. From the initial states, over the boundary inputs you allow at each time (default: every value), every run is explored breadth first up to `horizon` steps; the result lists the reachable states, the fixed points among them, and the runs that block (a state with no row for its inputs). `unsafe` decides escalation: reachable (with a shortest trace), unreachable (the reachable set stopped growing, so at no horizon), or unreachable-within-horizon. `safe` decides invariance: violated (shortest trace), invariant, or invariant-within-horizon. Without `inputs` the configurations are finite, so each verdict also carries `unbounded`, decided at every horizon by continuing the search past the horizon within the same state cap: reachable or violated (with the time and, past the horizon, a shortest trace), unreachable or invariant (with completeAfter), or undecided (cap-exceeded past the horizon, or blocked); the bounded verdict beside it is unchanged. A blocked state meets a target by its state conditions; a port condition there leaves the verdict undecided (reason blocked), never safe. `separation` takes two to four demands, each a target set with a time window, and decides whether one run visits each within its window (separation in time along a trajectory, Principle 15): realizable with a witness trace, unrealizable (a demand never met, or no single run meets them all), or undecided (a blocked run might meet them all). Without `inputs`, `loops` classifies the closed components (no step leaves them) of the reachable graph of the global states of boxes that declare transition, explored without a horizon up to the cap, from the initial states and every state meeting `safe`'s state conditions: bistable (fixed points in two or more closed components), trapped (a closed component every configuration of which meets `unsafe`: an absorbing trap, with a shortest trace into it), recurrent (a closed component that meets `unsafe` and also holds a safe configuration: the run can recover but never leaves it, with a shortest trace into it and the safe configuration), oscillating (a cycle and no fixed point, with its period and one cycle); each closed component reports `unsafe` (it meets the set) and `allUnsafe` (it lies inside it); classes can coexist, and 'none' means no closed component was found within the cap. Behavior rows are never read as transitions. Every trace is re-checked against the declared rows. With `certificate: true`, supported reachable escalations encode and prove their row-derived trace. State-only negative results encode a closed invariant, initial coverage, and unsafe exclusion or safe containment. Saturated unreachable port-target certificates instead exclude admitted unsafe configurations (Sync.target); they do not certify the absence of unsafe blocked states. When the bounded escalation is open and `unbounded` is decided, the certificate states the unbounded verdict (a trace past the horizon, or the unreachable invariant). Input schedules, bounded-only negatives, safe port predicates and loop-class certificates give an explicit unsupported reason. Certificates have source-bound manifests and require independent Lean checking. Fails closed on ill-typed rows, unknown targets, and past the state cap. Verdicts hold for the rows as declared; continuous dynamics, convergence rates, and control are not modelled.

tools.name: triz_feasibility
tools.description: Monotone co-design feasibility (Censi 2015) from declared box `feasibility` rows: each row provides a level per output port against the levels it requires per input port and an operating cost, read monotonically (providing less never needs more; more resources never hurt). Fails closed on ill-typed or dominated rows, a requirement no non-harmful function supplies, an extensive input fed by several functions (extensive-fan-in: model a merge box), and past the caps. No polynomial bound is claimed. The verdict holds for the rows as declared; the absorber's new harms are not modelled.

tools.name: triz_abstraction
tools.description: Check that a coarse function model (few boxes, e.g. with declared behaviour) is an abstraction of a detailed one of the same system (many boxes, e.g. with costs and feasibility) under a typed map: detailed box → coarse box (several may share one; a box left out is outside the abstraction), per box detailed port → coarse port (default: the same id and side), detailed carrier → coarse carrier (default: the same id). A function between two mapped ports is mapped; one between unmapped ports of boxes with the same image is hidden inside that coarse box; one between boxes with different images and an unmapped port is forgotten. Four checks: total (every mapped port's carrier has an image, and every mapped function has an image coarse function with the mapped endpoints, the mapped carrier, and the same polarity class: negative = harmful or excessive, or not), typed (each mapped port lands on a port of the same side whose carrier is its carrier's image, of the same layer; typed_map), wires (every coarse function is the image of a mapped detailed function of its class), harm loops (every coarse harm loop is the image of a detailed one: each harmful or excessive coarse function on it has such a preimage whose object reaches its performer along mapped and hidden functions; cycle_map, with the detailed cycle as witness). Verdict abstraction or not-an-abstraction with the failing checks. Also reports the functions hidden, forgotten, and left out (harms listed apart), the detailed harm loops the coarse model hides or loses, whether reachability among mapped boxes passes to the coarse model (reach_map, when nothing is forgotten), and, where a coarse box with behaviour has one preimage box with feasibility, whether that box's feasibility amounts read through the coarse carriers' levels fall in the coarse behaviour. When either model declares flows, each detailed flow's runs inside the mapped boxes are sent through the map like a merge and matched step by step against the coarse flows of the image carrier (flows.images), and coarse flow steps no detailed step maps to are listed (flows.unbacked); flows do not change the verdict. Fails closed on a model that does not type-check and on map ids that do not exist. Whether the coarse rows are true of their preimages is substantiated outside the kernel.

tools.name: triz_nine_windows
tools.description: System operator (9 windows) over function models: for past, present, and future, the subsystem view (restriction to the boxes you name, with crossing functions as its boundary), the system view, and the supersystem view (the tool and mediator boxes, or the boxes you list, collapsed into one black box; hidden harmful functions are listed). Each view reports its boxes, function counts, and harm loops. Present is required. Past and future are snapshots with stable box ids, or transitions: triz_transform operations applied in order (past_to_present needs past and must reach present; present_to_future must reach future if given, or derives it). A transition that fails or does not reach its snapshot fails closed. Each transition is reported as one net rewrite step, its part inside the subsystem (which takes the earlier subsystem view to the later one), whether it stays within the subsystem, and the boundary functions it cuts and adds. When the snapshots declare behaviour or feasibility, each time's system view carries its verdicts (system.verdicts) and each change between times says how they move (changes[].verdicts): behaviour compared as triz_behavior compare_to does, weakness ranked with `acceptable`, and feasibility, changed only when both sides are decided; a failure there never fails the grid. When the snapshots declare flows, the verdicts carry each flow's triz_flow candidates, and each change lists the flows added, removed, and re-routed and the candidates each flow gains or loses; a transition must reach the snapshot's flows too, and flowsChanged lists the flows it changes. Missing windows are reported as prompts.

tools.name: triz_queue

time_unit.description: Duration represented by one synchronous queue step, e.g. '1 ms'

quantity_unit.description: Discrete conserved unit, e.g. requests or packets

arrivals.description: Alternative arrival counts for EACH time slot; every combination is considered

service_capacity.description: Maximum units served per time slot

schedule.description: Specifies exactly when storage overflow is checked

tools.name: triz_conservation
tools.description: Check declared consumptive versus shared-level supply constraints for explicit units. Consumptive branches sum; shared intensive requirements use max. No physical law is inferred from labels.

inputs.description: Available amount, or shared intensive level

outputs.description: Simultaneous requested amounts, or minimum intensive levels

tools.name: triz_rule_set

left.description: L: what must be present; L \ K is deleted

right.description: R: what is there afterwards; R \ K is created under fresh ids

distinct.description: Pairs of carrier variables that must bind different carriers: an application condition, checked with the gluing conditions

forbid.description: Negative application conditions (Habel–Pennemann): each pattern extends `left` by id with the same constraints, and a match that extends to an occurrence of it — including any elements the pattern adds — is not applicable. tools.name: triz_trim_rewrite
tools.description: Return an applied trim as explicit deletion/gluing data with its declared absorbers, interface, and checked replay. No Kan-extension claim is made.

flows.description: Flow paths: which boxes a carrier passes through, in order. Read by triz_flow and by merge's adjacent reading; the other checks ignore them

weights.description: Explicit normalization to a scalar ideality: one weight per cost dimension plus 'harmful'

dimension.description: Unit, protocol, or measure carried, e.g. 'W thermal', 'gRPC request', 'USD/month'

values.description: Finite set of values the carrier can take, e.g. ['low', 'high']; required on every port of a box that declares behavior

levels.description: Thresholds that read a numeric amount (a feasibility row's level) as one of the declared values (a behavior row's value): an amount reads as the last level whose `from` it reaches. The list orders its values from least to most; the first starts at 0 and each `from` exceeds the one before. Requires values, e.g. [{ value: 'low', from: 0 }, { value: 'high', from: 50 }]

quantity.description: How amounts on this carrier combine where one output port feeds several functions. 'intensive' (the default) is one shared level, such as a voltage, a temperature, or a copied message: the port meets the largest demand. 'extensive' is an amount that divides, such as a flow of water or a current: triz_feasibility makes the port supply the sum of the demands, and refuses an extensive input fed by several functions (model a merge box). Declare it explicitly; it is never inferred from the layer

loss.description: Whether the flow is a loss: true when no level of it is wanted from any performer, such as a pressure drop, leakage, noise, or wear; false when some level is. Read only by the defect-on-loss-carrier lint, which then ignores its word list, so the lint gives the same warnings after any renaming. Omitted, the lint guesses from the words of the carrier id, its dimension, and the function verbs. No verdict reads it

value.description: A declared value of the carrier

from.description: Least amount that reads as this value, in the units of the feasibility rows on this carrier

role.description: Function-analysis role; environment and supersystem boxes are resources outside the engineered system

inner.description: Nested model and explicit one-to-one outer-to-inner interface bindings

cost.description: Cost per resource dimension, e.g. { usd_month: 400, latency_ms: 2.5 }; dimensions are never summed together

behavior.description: Declared behaviour: a finite relation from input-port values to output-port values over the carriers' declared values. An input tuple with no row cannot occur; several rows for one input tuple are alternatives. Omit when unknown

producible.description: For a box whose behaviour is unknown: the rows it can physically produce, over the carriers' declared values, as behavior rows. triz_behavior weakest_spec keeps only these, and reports the rows the target needs that the box cannot produce. A box declares behavior or producible, not both

state.description: Declared state: the finite set of values the box carries from one step to the next. Requires transition

initial.description: States the box may start in; a subset of state

transition.description: Declared dynamics: rows (state, inputs) → (next state, outputs) over the declared state and carrier values, making the box a nondeterministic Mealy machine. A (state, inputs) pair with no row cannot occur; several rows are alternatives. Requires state; a box declares behavior or transition, not both

feasibility.description: Monotone co-design feasibility: the minimal rows the box can work at, each a level provided per output port against the levels it requires per input port and its operating cost. Read monotonically: providing less never needs more, and more resources never hurt. No row may be dominated by another. An output port of an intensive carrier has one level shared by every function on it; on an extensive carrier (`quantity`) the demands of its functions add up. Omit when unknown

tools.description: Optional project extension: analyse an OTSM Network of Problems (contradiction graph) and its verifier-backed purpose gates. A node may carry a PhysicalContradiction; each is checked by separationCheck (irreducible, separable, no-contradiction, or invalid, which fails closed for that node), and the core-conflict ranking breaks ties on dissolves in favour of irreducible nodes and flags a top node that already separates.
